description: The people behind the people. AForce is supported by operators who have built, scaled, and exited at the highest level — Peter Ingwersen (brand strategy), Kristel van Kleef (retail and go-to-market), Mark Mendel (investment banking, Finalis), and Thomas Masterbouni (CIO, Big Idea Ventures).

description: Performance hydration is evolving beyond energy into readiness, recovery, and daily ritual. Illustrative market size.

description: Monster. Celsius. Prime. Ghost. Gatorade. Every brand competes for attention. Few compete for composure.

title: The White Space
description: AForce owns the moment before execution. The full product lineup floating in the white space the category left empty.

title: The Ritual
description: Pause. Hydrate. Lock in. Perform. Four beats. No explanation.

title: The System
description: Products create acquisition. The OS creates retention. Hydration to community.

title: The Framework
description: Seven steps. One compounding system. Product, ritual, behavior, OS, retention, membership, scale — each step earns the next. None can be skipped.

title: The Moat
description: The more you use AForce, the harder it becomes to leave. Performance data. Streak psychology. Identity formation.

title: The Proof Engine
description: Miami and Brickell provide a concentrated population of high-performance consumers.

title: Road To America's Real Deal
description: Soft launch. Proof of concept. Community scale. National television.

title: Why AForce Wins
description: Competitors each own one category — Gatorade sports performance, Liquid I.V. functional hydration, LMNT electrolytes, AG1 daily wellness, WHOOP recovery. AForce owns Quiet Performance: preparation, discipline, recovery, consistency, readiness.

title: Why Invest Today
description: Friends & family investors enter before institutional capital. Four pillars: patent-protected technology, national retail rollout, media momentum (America's Real Deal on Prime), and a tens-of-billions market.

title: The Terms
description: Friends & family investment terms and equity breakdown. Minimum investment $25,000 via SAFE; tiered equity from 0.125% to 1.00%; projected investor returns across exit valuations. Illustrative.

title: Use of Funds
description: How capital will be deployed: 40% inventory & production, 20% sales & distribution, 15% marketing & brand, 10% team & operations, 10% working capital, 5% legal/compliance/IP.

title: Roadmap to the Next Valuation
description: 24-month roadmap: 2026 retail launch, 2027 multi-state growth and institutional discussions, 2028 national footprint and strategic options. Value creation ladder from friends & family round to strategic exit.

title: The Comparable
description: BodyArmor proved the upside — founded 2011, acquired by Coca-Cola for $5.6B in 2021, early investors saw 100x+ returns. What a comparable AForce outcome could mean for early investors. Illustrative.

title: The Exit
description: AForce is a prime strategic acquisition target. Category comps: Prime $250M+ year one, Liquid I.V. $500M to Unilever, BodyArmor $5.6B to Coca-Cola, Oatly $10B+ IPO.

title: The Close
description: Every layer compounds the last. The product creates entry, the ritual creates behavior, the OS creates retention, the membership creates recurring revenue, the ecosystem creates scale. Identity to Ritual to Behavior to OS to Retention to Membership to Scale.
